To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the catalytic domain (D) of DAF (A) was fused with amphotropic MuLV envelope (F) and the resulting fusion protein was expressed in murine helper cells.

the catalytic domain (DAF) of the human complement regulating protein decay accelerating factor (DAF), when fused to the envelope (Env) protein of the amphotoptic murine leukemia virus 4070A, confers protection against the human complement system to amphotropic retroviral vectors.
a murine retrovirus with a human complement regulatory protein fused to its envelope protein exhibits strong protection against the human complement system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a new class of retroviral vectors that are protected against the human complement system and therefore can be used for human gene therapy.
the production of retroviruses that are protected against the human complement system.
the generation and characterization of complement-protected amphotopic retroviruses from NIH 3 T 3 packaging cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of DAF in the form of the fusion protein DAFF-2A in combination with amphotropic MuLV 4070A Env protein results in a stable and efficient production of complement-resistant retroviral vectors.
the fusion protein DAFF-EnvA protects the virions from the human complement system, but the mechanism of this protection has yet to be determined.
DAFF2A virions are protected against human complement attack and are thus suitable for in vivo gene transfer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel method for generating complement-protected retroviral vectors that are suitable for human in vivo application.
the fusion of the catalytic DAF domain to the envelope protein of amphotropic murid leukemia viruses can be used to generate retroviruses that are protected from human complement attack.

the catalytic domain from the human complement regulatory proteins DAF, MCP and CD 59 can be fused to the amphotropic Env protein without loss of viral infectivity, but only DAF confers protection of the virions against human complement attack.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the membrane of retroviruses can be modified with human complement regulators.
we were able to protect murine amphotropic retrovirus from human complement attack by fusing the catalytic domain from the human complement regulatory factor decay-accelerated factor (DAF).
we have generated amphotropic retroviral particles that are protected from complement attack in human serum.
